4	  - Affine associative scan: manually tiled for TPU MXU
5	  - Expert gather: fused gather for dynamic scatter-gather patterns

8	the input size is too small to benefit from custom tiling.

10	NOTE: Pallas APIs change frequently. All Pallas calls are wrapped in
11	try/except to gracefully fall back to pure JAX on API incompatibility.
12	"""

25	def _associative_combine(left, right):
26	    """Binary operator for 2x2 affine associative scan.
27	
28	    Combines (M_left, b_left) and (M_right, b_right):
29	      M_combined = M_right @ M_left
30	      b_combined = M_right @ b_left + b_right
31	    """
32	    M_left, b_left = left
33	    M_right, b_right = right
34	
35	    # M_combined = M_right @ M_left (2x2 matmul)
36	    M_combined = jnp.einsum('...ij,...jk->...ik', M_right, M_left)
37	
38	    # b_combined = M_right @ b_left + b_right
39	    b_combined = jnp.einsum('...ij,...j->...i', M_right, b_left) + b_right
40	
41	    return M_combined, b_combined

44	if _HAS_PALLAS:
45	    def pallas_affine_scan(Ms, bs, N, d_inner):
46	        """Pallas-optimized 2x2 affine associative scan.
47	
48	        The binary operator combines (M_left, b_left) with (M_right, b_right):
49	          M_combined = M_right @ M_left
50	          b_combined = M_right @ b_left + b_right
51	
52	        Pallas tiles the scan into chunks that fit in VMEM, with
53	        the 2x2 matmul mapped to MXU tile operations.
54	
55	        Args:
56	            Ms: [N, 2, 2] array of 2x2 matrices
57	            bs: [N, 2] array of 2-vectors
58	            N: number of timesteps
59	            d_inner: inner dimension (unused, for API compat)

61	        Returns:
62	            (M_out, b_out): prefix scan results
63	        """

65	        def scan_kernel(M_ref, b_ref, M_out_ref, b_out_ref):
66	            """Pallas kernel body -- processes one tile of the scan."""
67	            M = M_ref[...]  # [tile_size, 2, 2]
68	            b = b_ref[...]  # [tile_size, 2]
69	
70	            # Sequential scan within tile (tile is small enough for VMEM)
71	            tile_size = M.shape[0]

73	            def scan_body(carry, inputs):
74	                prev_M, prev_b = carry
75	                curr_M, curr_b = inputs
76

78	                new_M = jnp.einsum('ij,jk->ik', curr_M, prev_M)
79	                # b_combined = curr_M @ prev_b + curr_b
80	                new_b = jnp.einsum('ij,j->i', curr_M, prev_b) + curr_b

296	    h_tilde = jnp.tanh(Wh @ x_reset + bh)

347	        peer_query_Ws, prod_keys_A, prod_keys_B,
348	        expert_W1, expert_b1, expert_W2, expert_b2,
349	        rescale, num_heads, pk_dim, gru_hidden, expert_hidden, num_experts,
350	        d_model
351	    ):
352	        """Pallas fused GRU+PEER kernel for TPU.
353	
354	        Fuses steps 2-4 of the fused_elem pipeline:
355	          2. GRU state update
356	          3. Multi-head PEER routing + Expert MLP
357	          4. Smart gradient computation
358	
359	        On TPU, this runs as a single Pallas kernel, keeping all
360	        intermediate values in VMEM/registers instead of HBM.
361	
362	        Args:
363	            grad: [N] gradient values
364	            sharpness: [N] sharpness metrics
365	            fwd_ctx: [N, d_model] forward scan context
366	            bwd_ctx: [N, d_model] backward scan context
367	            gru_state: [N, gru_hidden] GRU hidden state
368	            gru_Wz/bz/Wr/br/Wh/bh: GRU weights
369	            peer_query_Ws: [num_heads, d_model, peer_input_dim]
370	            prod_keys_A/B: [num_heads, pk_dim, d_model//2]
371	            expert_W1/b1/W2/b2: expert MLP weights
372	            rescale: scaling factor for meta-net output
373	            Various dimension params.
374	
375	        Returns:
376	            smart_grad: [N] smart-weighted gradients
377	            gru_state_new: [N, gru_hidden] updated GRU states

379	        N = grad.shape[0]
380	        peer_input_dim = d_model * 2 + gru_hidden + 2  # fwd, bwd, h, g, s
381	
382	        def fused_kernel(
383	            grad_ref, sharpness_ref, fwd_ctx_ref, bwd_ctx_ref,
384	            gru_state_ref,
385	            smart_grad_ref, gru_state_out_ref
386	        ):
387	            """Pallas kernel body — processes one tile of elements."""
388	            tile_size = grad_ref.shape[0]
389	
390	            for elem in range(tile_size):
391	                g = grad_ref[elem]
392	                s = sharpness_ref[elem]
393	                fc = fwd_ctx_ref[elem]  # [d_model]
394	                bc = bwd_ctx_ref[elem]  # [d_model]
395	                h_old = gru_state_ref[elem]  # [gru_hidden]
396	
397	                # Build GRU input: [g, s, fwd_ctx, bwd_ctx, h_old]
398	                x_input = jnp.concatenate([
399	                    jnp.array([g, s]), fc, bc, h_old
400	                ])
401	
402	                # GRU update
403	                h_new = _gru_update_jax(
404	                    h_old, x_input, gru_Wz, gru_bz, gru_Wr, gru_br,
405	                    gru_Wh, gru_bh, gru_hidden)
406	
407	                # Build PEER query input: [h_new, fwd_ctx, bwd_ctx, g, s]
408	                query_input = jnp.concatenate([h_new, fc, bc, jnp.array([g, s])])
409	
410	                # PEER routing + expert MLP
411	                total_out = _peer_routing_jax(
412	                    query_input, peer_query_Ws, prod_keys_A, prod_keys_B,
413	                    expert_W1, expert_b1, expert_W2, expert_b2,
414	                    num_heads, pk_dim, expert_hidden, num_experts, g)
415	
416	                # Smart gradient
417	                smart_grad_ref[elem] = g + rescale * (total_out / num_heads)
418	                gru_state_out_ref[elem] = h_new
419	
420	        TILE = min(64, N)
421	
422	        try:
423	            smart_grad, gru_state_new = pl.pallas_call(
424	                fused_kernel,
425	                out_shape=[
426	                    jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((N,), grad.dtype),
427	                    jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((N, gru_hidden), gru_state.dtype),
428	                ],
429	                grid=(N // TILE,),
430	                in_specs=[
431	                    # BlockSpec index_map returns BLOCK indices (block i covers
432	                    # rows [i*TILE:(i+1)*TILE]), so the map must be ``i`` — not
433	                    # the element offset ``i*TILE`` which over-runs the grid
434	                    # (tiles >=2 read out-of-bounds -> silently wrong / NaN).
435	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE,), lambda i: (i,)),
436	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE,), lambda i: (i,)),
437	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, d_model), lambda i: (i, 0)),
438	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, d_model), lambda i: (i, 0)),
439	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, gru_hidden), lambda i: (i, 0)),
440	                ],
441	                out_specs=[
442	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE,), lambda i: (i,)),
443	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, gru_hidden), lambda i: (i, 0)),
444	                ],
445	            )(grad, sharpness, fwd_ctx, bwd_ctx, gru_state)
446	
447	            return smart_grad, gru_state_new
448	
449	        except Exception:
450	            # Pallas API incompatibility — fall through to pure JAX vmap
451	            pass
452	
453	        return _fused_gru_peer_jax(
454	            grad, sharpness, fwd_ctx, bwd_ctx, gru_state,
455	            gru_Wz, gru_bz, gru_Wr, gru_br, gru_Wh, gru_bh,
456	            peer_query_Ws, prod_keys_A, prod_keys_B,
457	            expert_W1, expert_b1, expert_W2, expert_b2,
458	            rescale, num_heads, pk_dim, gru_hidden, expert_hidden,

463	    grad, sharpness, fwd_ctx, bwd_ctx, gru_state,
464	    gru_Wz, gru_bz, gru_Wr, gru_br, gru_Wh, gru_bh,
465	    peer_query_Ws, prod_keys_A, prod_keys_B,
466	    expert_W1, expert_b1, expert_W2, expert_b2,
467	    rescale, num_heads, pk_dim, gru_hidden, expert_hidden,
468	    num_experts, d_model

475	        s = sharpness[i]

477	        bc = bwd_ctx[i]
478	        h_old = gru_state[i]

481	        h_new = _gru_update_jax(

489	            num_heads, pk_dim, expert_hidden, num_experts, g)

494	    # Vectorize over elements
495	    smart_grads, gru_states_new = jax.vmap(

497	    )(jnp.arange(N))

558	def _make_pallas_scan_kernel(tile_size: int):
559	    """Build a Pallas scan kernel closure for the given MXU tile width.
560	
561	    The returned kernel performs a tiled parallel prefix scan using
562	    Affine2x2 composition.  Each grid block processes ``tile_size``
563	    consecutive (M, b) pairs using ``jax.lax.scan`` inside VMEM, and
564	    a subsequent cross-tile ``jax.lax.associative_scan`` stitches the
565	    tiles together.
566	
567	    Args:
568	        tile_size: Number of timesteps per Pallas tile (128 or 256).
569	
570	    Returns:
571	        A function ``(Ms, bs) -> (M_out, b_out)`` implementing the
572	        full prefix scan.
573	    """
574	    TILE = tile_size
575	
576	    def _tiled_scan(Ms, bs):
577	        """Run tiled affine prefix scan with tile_size=TILE.
578	
579	        Args:
580	            Ms: [N, 2, 2] affine matrices.
581	            bs: [N, 2] bias vectors.
582	
583	        Returns:
584	            Tuple of prefix-scanned (Ms_out, bs_out) with the same shapes.
585	        """
586	        N = Ms.shape[0]
587	
588	        # Small inputs: fall back to pure JAX associative scan
589	        if N <= TILE:
590	            return jax.lax.associative_scan(_associative_combine, (Ms, bs))
591	
592	        # Pad N to a multiple of TILE so the grid divides evenly
593	        remainder = N % TILE
594	        if remainder != 0:
595	            pad_len = TILE - remainder
596	            Ms = jnp.concatenate([
597	                Ms, jnp.tile(jnp.eye(2, dtype=Ms.dtype)[None], (pad_len, 1, 1))
598	            ], axis=0)
599	            bs = jnp.concatenate([
600	                bs, jnp.zeros((pad_len, 2), dtype=bs.dtype)
601	            ], axis=0)
602	            N_padded = N + pad_len
603	        else:
604	            N_padded = N
605	            pad_len = 0
606	
607	        num_tiles = N_padded // TILE
608	
609	        def scan_kernel(M_ref, b_ref, M_out_ref, b_out_ref):
610	            """Pallas kernel body — sequential scan within one tile."""
611	            M = M_ref[...]   # [TILE, 2, 2]
612	            b = b_ref[...]   # [TILE, 2]
613	
614	            def scan_body(carry, inputs):
615	                prev_M, prev_b = carry
616	                curr_M, curr_b = inputs
617	                new_M = jnp.einsum('ij,jk->ik', curr_M, prev_M)
618	                new_b = jnp.einsum('ij,j->i', curr_M, prev_b) + curr_b
619	                return (new_M, new_b), (new_M, new_b)
620	
621	            init_M = jnp.eye(2, dtype=M.dtype)
622	            init_b = jnp.zeros(2, dtype=b.dtype)
623	
624	            _, (scanned_M, scanned_b) = jax.lax.scan(
625	                scan_body, (init_M, init_b), (M, b))
626	
627	            M_out_ref[...] = scanned_M
628	            b_out_ref[...] = scanned_b
629	
630	        if not _HAS_PALLAS:
631	            return jax.lax.associative_scan(_associative_combine, (Ms[:N], bs[:N]))
632	
633	        try:
634	            M_out, b_out = pl.pallas_call(
635	                scan_kernel,
636	                out_shape=[
637	                    jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(Ms.shape, Ms.dtype),
638	                    jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(bs.shape, bs.dtype),
639	                ],
640	                grid=(num_tiles,),
641	                in_specs=[
642	                    # BlockSpec index_map returns BLOCK indices, not element
643	                    # offsets: block i covers rows [i*TILE : (i+1)*TILE]. Using
644	                    # ``i * TILE`` here pointed past the array for grid step
645	                    # i>=1 (only block 0 landed), leaving tiles 2..K reading/
646	                    # writing out-of-bounds blocks — silently wrong (NaN in
647	                    # interpret mode) for N > 2*TILE. Must be ``i``.
648	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, 2, 2), lambda i: (i, 0, 0)),
649	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, 2), lambda i: (i, 0)),
650	                ],
651	                out_specs=[
652	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, 2, 2), lambda i: (i, 0, 0)),
653	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, 2), lambda i: (i, 0)),
654	                ],
655	            )(Ms, bs)
656	        except Exception:
657	            # Pallas API mismatch — pure JAX fallback
658	            if pad_len > 0:
659	                Ms = Ms[:N]
660	                bs = bs[:N]
661	            return jax.lax.associative_scan(_associative_combine, (Ms, bs))
662	
663	        # ── Cross-tile reduction ─────────────────────────────────
664	        # Collect last element of each tile as the tile summary.
665	        tile_summary_Ms = M_out[TILE - 1::TILE]   # [num_tiles, 2, 2]
666	        tile_summary_bs = b_out[TILE - 1::TILE]   # [num_tiles, 2]
667	
668	        prefix_Ms, prefix_bs = jax.lax.associative_scan(
669	            _associative_combine, (tile_summary_Ms, tile_summary_bs))
670	
671	        # ── Apply correction to each tile (tile 0 needs no correction) ──
672	        # Reshape into [num_tiles, TILE, ...] for vectorised correction.
673	        M_tiles = M_out.reshape(num_tiles, TILE, 2, 2)
674	        b_tiles = b_out.reshape(num_tiles, TILE, 2)
675	
676	        # Build per-tile prefix: tile 0 gets identity, tiles 1..K get
677	        # prefix_Ms[0..K-1] / prefix_bs[0..K-1].
678	        identity_M = jnp.eye(2, dtype=Ms.dtype)[None]  # [1, 2, 2]
679	        zero_b = jnp.zeros((1, 2), dtype=bs.dtype)      # [1, 2]
680	        correction_Ms = jnp.concatenate([identity_M, prefix_Ms[:-1]], axis=0)  # [num_tiles, 2, 2]
681	        correction_bs = jnp.concatenate([zero_b, prefix_bs[:-1]], axis=0)      # [num_tiles, 2]
682	
683	        # Vectorised correction: M_new = M_elem @ corr_M, b_new = M_elem @ corr_b + b_elem.
684	        # ``correction_Ms`` is [num_tiles, 2, 2] (one prefix per tile); it
685	        # broadcasts over the within-tile axis ``t`` via the shared ``n`` index.
686	        # (The former ``correction_Ms[:, None, :, :]`` made the operand rank-4,
687	        # which mismatched the rank-3 ``njk`` subscript and always raised.)
688	        corrected_Ms = jnp.einsum('ntij,njk->ntik', M_tiles, correction_Ms)
689	        corrected_bs = jnp.einsum('ntij,nj->nti', M_tiles, correction_bs) + b_tiles
690	
691	        result_Ms = corrected_Ms.reshape(N_padded, 2, 2)[:N]
692	        result_bs = corrected_bs.reshape(N_padded, 2)[:N]
693	
694	        return result_Ms, result_bs
695	
696	    return _tiled_scan
697

737	def vmem_persistent_expert_mlp(
738	    x, expert_W1, expert_b1, expert_W2, expert_b2,
739	    expert_indices, top_k, tpu_version=None,
740	):
741	    """Expert MLP with VMEM-persistent weights on v5p/v6e TPUs.
742	
743	    On TPU v5p and v6e the expert weight tiles are loaded into VMEM
744	    with ``eviction_policy="none"`` so they remain resident across
745	    loop iterations, eliminating repeated HBM round-trips for hot
746	    experts.
747	
748	    On older TPUs (v4/v5e) or when Pallas is unavailable, this falls
749	    back to a standard ``jnp.take`` gather followed by a batched MLP.
750	
751	    Args:
752	        x: [batch, d_model] input activations.
753	        expert_W1: [num_experts, expert_hidden, d_model] first linear weights.
754	        expert_b1: [num_experts, expert_hidden] first linear bias.
755	        expert_W2: [num_experts, d_model, expert_hidden] second linear weights.
756	        expert_b2: [num_experts, d_model] second linear bias.
757	        expert_indices: [batch, top_k] selected expert indices per token.
758	        top_k: number of experts per token.
759	        tpu_version: optional override; auto-detected if None.
760	
761	    Returns:
762	        y: [batch, d_model] expert MLP output (sum over top_k experts).
763	    """
764	    if tpu_version is None:
765	        tpu_version = detect_tpu_version()
766	
767	    batch_size = x.shape[0]
768	    d_model = x.shape[1]
769	    num_experts = expert_W1.shape[0]
770	    expert_hidden = expert_W1.shape[1]
771	
772	    use_vmem = (tpu_version in ("v5p", "v6e")) and _HAS_PALLAS
773	
774	    if use_vmem:
775	        # ── Pallas kernel with VMEM-persistent expert weights ─────
776	        TILE = min(64, batch_size)
777	        num_blocks = max(1, batch_size // TILE)
778	
779	        def vmem_expert_kernel(
780	            x_ref, indices_ref,
781	            W1_ref, b1_ref, W2_ref, b2_ref,
782	            y_ref,
783	        ):
784	            """Pallas kernel: load expert weights into VMEM once."""
785	            tile_x = x_ref[...]          # [TILE, d_model]
786	            tile_idx = indices_ref[...]   # [TILE, top_k]
787	
788	            # Accumulate results for the tile
789	            tile_y = jnp.zeros_like(tile_x)
790	
791	            for k in range(top_k):
792	                for elem in range(TILE):
793	                    eidx = tile_idx[elem, k]
794	                    # Load with eviction_policy="none" to keep in VMEM
795	                    w1 = pl.load(W1_ref, (eidx,), eviction_policy="none")  # [expert_hidden, d_model]
796	                    b1 = pl.load(b1_ref, (eidx,), eviction_policy="none")  # [expert_hidden]
797	                    w2 = pl.load(W2_ref, (eidx,), eviction_policy="none")  # [d_model, expert_hidden]
798	                    b2 = pl.load(b2_ref, (eidx,), eviction_policy="none")  # [d_model]
799	
800	                    xi = tile_x[elem]                                # [d_model]
801	                    hidden = jax.nn.gelu(w1 @ xi + b1)               # [expert_hidden]
802	                    out = w2 @ hidden + b2                           # [d_model]
803	                    tile_y = tile_y.at[elem].add(out)
804	
805	            y_ref[...] = tile_y
806	
807	        try:
808	            y = pl.pallas_call(
809	                vmem_expert_kernel,
810	                out_shape=[
811	                    jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((batch_size, d_model), x.dtype),
812	                ],
813	                grid=(num_blocks,),
814	                in_specs=[
815	                    # BlockSpec index_map returns BLOCK indices (block i covers
816	                    # rows [i*TILE:(i+1)*TILE]), so the map must be ``i`` — not
817	                    # the element offset ``i*TILE`` which over-runs the grid
818	                    # (tiles >=2 read out-of-bounds -> silently wrong / NaN).
819	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, d_model), lambda i: (i, 0)),
820	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, top_k), lambda i: (i, 0)),
821	                    # Expert weight tables — full arrays, no tiling
822	                    pl.BlockSpec((num_experts, expert_hidden, d_model), lambda i: (0, 0, 0)),
823	                    pl.BlockSpec((num_experts, expert_hidden), lambda i: (0, 0)),
824	                    pl.BlockSpec((num_experts, d_model, expert_hidden), lambda i: (0, 0, 0)),
825	                    pl.BlockSpec((num_experts, d_model), lambda i: (0, 0)),
826	                ],
827	                out_specs=[
828	                    pl.BlockSpec((TILE, d_model), lambda i: (i, 0)),
829	                ],
830	            )(x, expert_indices, expert_W1, expert_b1, expert_W2, expert_b2)
831	            return y
832	        except Exception:
833	            # Pallas API incompatibility — fall through to pure JAX fallback
834	            pass

856	def sharded_mamba3_scan(Ms, bs, mesh, axis_name='dp', tile_size=128):
857	    """Multi-device sharded affine prefix scan using shard_map.
858	
859	    Implements a 3-phase parallel prefix scan across multiple TPU chips:
860	      1. **Local scan** — each device runs an independent prefix scan on
861	         its shard of the sequence.
862	      2. **Summary prefix** — the last element of each local scan forms
863	         a summary.  These summaries are gathered, prefix-scanned, and
864	         scattered back.
865	      3. **Correction** — each device applies the incoming prefix from
866	         all preceding devices to its local results.
867	
868	    Args:
869	        Ms: [N, 2, 2] affine matrices (sharded along axis 0 across
870	            the mesh's ``axis_name``).
871	        bs: [N, 2] bias vectors (same sharding).
872	        mesh: ``jax.sharding.Mesh`` spanning the devices.
873	        axis_name: name of the mesh axis used for data parallelism.
874	        tile_size: MXU tile width forwarded to the per-device Pallas
875	            scan kernel (128 for v4/v5, 256 for v6e).
876	
877	    Returns:
878	        Tuple of prefix-scanned (Ms_out, bs_out).
879	    """
880	    num_devices = mesh.shape[axis_name]
881	    local_scan_fn = _make_pallas_scan_kernel(tile_size)
882	
883	    if num_devices <= 1 or not _HAS_SHARD_MAP:
884	        # Single device — just run local scan
885	        return local_scan_fn(Ms, bs)
886	
887	    def _sharded_scan_body(Ms_shard, bs_shard):
888	        """Runs on each device inside shard_map.
889	
890	        Phase 1: local prefix scan.
891	        Phase 2: all-gather summaries, prefix-scan across devices,
892	                 extract this device's incoming correction.
893	        Phase 3: apply correction to local results.
894	        """
895	        # Phase 1 — local scan
896	        local_Ms, local_bs = local_scan_fn(Ms_shard, bs_shard)
897	
898	        # Phase 2 — cross-device prefix
899	        # Summary = last element of the local scan
900	        summary_M = local_Ms[-1:]  # [1, 2, 2]
901	        summary_b = local_bs[-1:]  # [1, 2]
902	
903	        # All-gather summaries across devices
904	        all_summary_Ms = jax.lax.all_gather(summary_M, axis_name=axis_name, axis=0)  # [num_devices, 2, 2]
905	        all_summary_bs = jax.lax.all_gather(summary_b, axis_name=axis_name, axis=0)  # [num_devices, 2]
906	
907	        # Squeeze the middle dim from all_gather
908	        all_summary_Ms = all_summary_Ms.reshape(-1, 2, 2)
909	        all_summary_bs = all_summary_bs.reshape(-1, 2)
910	
911	        # Prefix scan on summaries
912	        prefix_Ms, prefix_bs = jax.lax.associative_scan(
913	            _associative_combine, (all_summary_Ms, all_summary_bs))
914	
915	        # Which device am I?  Use axis_index.
916	        device_idx = jax.lax.axis_index(axis_name)
917	
918	        # Correction for this device: prefix from (device_idx - 1), or identity
919	        corr_M = jnp.where(
920	            device_idx > 0,
921	            prefix_Ms[device_idx - 1],
922	            jnp.eye(2, dtype=Ms_shard.dtype),
923	        )
924	        corr_b = jnp.where(
925	            device_idx > 0,
926	            prefix_bs[device_idx - 1],
927	            jnp.zeros(2, dtype=bs_shard.dtype),
928	        )
929	
930	        # Phase 3 — apply correction: M_new = M_local @ corr_M,
931	        #           b_new = M_local @ corr_b + b_local
932	        corrected_Ms = jnp.einsum('nij,jk->nik', local_Ms, corr_M)
933	        corrected_bs = jnp.einsum('nij,j->ni', local_Ms, corr_b) + local_bs
934	
935	        return corrected_Ms, corrected_bs
936	
937	    in_specs = (P(axis_name), P(axis_name))
938	    out_specs = (P(axis_name), P(axis_name))
939	
940	    sharded_fn = shard_map(
941	        _sharded_scan_body,
942	        mesh=mesh,
943	        in_specs=in_specs,
944	        out_specs=out_specs,
945	        check_rep=False,
946	    )

948	    return sharded_fn(Ms, bs)

137	    def muon_adamw_update(params, grads, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, step,
138	                          beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98, lr=1e-3, wd=1.0, eps=1e-8):
139	        # Real Muon for the fused composition. The fused param tree STACKS the
140	        # per-layer parameters, so a single leaf here is rank-1 (a bias vector),
141	        # rank-2 (one weight matrix), or rank-3+ (a STACK of per-layer weight
142	        # matrices). Muon orthogonalizes each 2-D matrix; we treat the LAST TWO
143	        # axes as the matrix and BATCH the Newton-Schulz iteration over any
144	        # leading (layer) axes via jnp.matmul's native batching, a batched
145	        # transpose (swapaxes(-1,-2)), and a PER-matrix Frobenius norm.
146	        #
147	        # History: the original stub applied plain AdamW and never
148	        # orthogonalized (not Muon at all). Delegating to the per-tensor
149	        # ``launch_muon_step`` then broke lowering, because its full-transpose
150	        # ``X.T`` and GLOBAL Frobenius norm are valid only for a single 2-D
151	        # matrix — on the rank-3 stacked tree ``X.T`` reverses the layer axis
152	        # and the matmul shapes become incompatible. The batched form below is
153	        # the real Muon orthogonalization that is also correct on the stack.
154	        #
155	        # Muon's state is one SGD-momentum buffer (carried in ``exp_avg``);
156	        # ``exp_avg_sq`` is passed through untouched (Muon has no second
157	        # moment). ``beta1`` is Muon's momentum; ``wd`` is decoupled decay.
158	        g = grads.astype(jnp.float32)
159	        new_buf = beta1 * exp_avg + g
160	        p = params.astype(jnp.float32)
161	        if params.ndim >= 2:
162	            mm = functools.partial(
163	                jnp.matmul, precision=jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST,
164	                preferred_element_type=jnp.float32)
165	            # Per-matrix Frobenius norm over the last two axes (keepdims so it
166	            # broadcasts across any leading stacked-layer axes).
167	            frob = jnp.sqrt(jnp.sum(new_buf * new_buf, axis=(-2, -1),
168	                                    keepdims=True)) + 1e-8
169	            X = new_buf / frob
170	            # Muon quintic NS coefficients (Jordan et al. 2024) — same as
171	            # launch_muon.newton_schulz_iterate, but batched over leading axes.
172	            a, b, c = 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315
173	            for _ in range(5):
174	                Xt = jnp.swapaxes(X, -1, -2)
175	                AX = mm(Xt, X)        # Xᵀ X           (batched n×n)
176	                AAX = mm(AX, AX)      # (Xᵀ X)²
177	                X = a * X + b * mm(X, AX) + c * mm(X, AAX)
178	            max_dim = max(params.shape[-1], params.shape[-2])
179	            neg_lr_scale = -lr * 0.2 * jnp.sqrt(jnp.float32(max_dim))
180	            new_p = p * (1.0 - lr * wd) + neg_lr_scale * X
181	        else:
182	            new_p = p - lr * new_buf
183	        return new_p, new_buf, exp_avg_sq

271	    def sg2_update(params, grads, state, meta_weights, hyperparams):
272	        """SuperGrok v2 step via the launcher's ``meta_net_forward`` + AdamW
273	        tail. Consumes/returns the fused dict-state contract."""
274	        g = grads.astype(jnp.float32)
275	        layer_beta1 = hyperparams["layer_beta1"]
276	        beta2 = hyperparams["beta2"]
277	        lr = hyperparams["lr"]
278	        wd = hyperparams["wd"]
279	        eps = hyperparams["eps"]
280	        lamb = hyperparams.get("lamb", 2.0)
281	        ramp = hyperparams.get("ramp", 1.0)
282	        gate_signal = hyperparams.get("gate_signal", 0.0)
283	        grad_clip = hyperparams.get("grad_clip", 1.0)
284	        # alpha_i is BOTH the slow-EMA decay and the mu/slow mixing coefficient
285	        # (supergrok2.py _single_param_step:2379/2405; supergrok2.h:388-394).
286	        alpha = hyperparams.get("alpha", 0.98)
287	
288	        exp_avg = state["exp_avg"]
289	        exp_avg_sq = state["exp_avg_sq"]
290	        mu = state["mu"]
291	        slow = state["slow"]
292	        sharpness = state["sharpness"]
293	        gru_state = state["gru_state"]
294	        step = state["step"]
295	
296	        gnorm = jnp.linalg.norm(g.reshape(-1))
297	        clip = jnp.minimum(1.0, grad_clip / (gnorm + 1e-12))
298	        gc = g * clip
299	
300	        meta_config = MetaNetConfig(
301	            d_model=meta_weights["d_model"], n_heads=meta_weights["n_heads"],
302	            csa_compress=meta_weights["csa_compress"],
303	            csa_window=meta_weights["csa_window"],
304	            csa_topk=meta_weights["csa_topk"],
305	            hca_compress=meta_weights["hca_compress"],
306	            indexer_rank=meta_weights["indexer_rank"],
307	            num_peer_heads=meta_weights["num_peer_heads"],
308	            num_experts=meta_weights["expert_W1"].shape[0],
309	            expert_hidden=meta_weights["expert_W1"].shape[1],
310	            gru_hidden=meta_weights["gru_hidden"],
311	            pk_dim=meta_weights["product_keys_A"].shape[1],
312	            rescale=meta_weights["rescale"],
313	        )
314	        mnw = _meta_weights_from_dict(meta_weights)
315	        smart_g, new_gru, _ = meta_net_forward(
316	            gc.reshape(-1), sharpness.reshape(-1), gru_state, mnw, meta_config,
317	        )
318	        smart_g = smart_g.reshape(g.shape)
319	
320	        # Restored grokfast amplification — byte-faithful to the authoritative
321	        # eager path supergrok2.py::_single_param_step:2394-2406 (and the kernel
322	        # tail csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h::sg2_apply_step:423-426):
323	        #   slow_new   = alpha*slow + (1-alpha)*g       (dedicated slow-grad EMA)
324	        #   lamb_eff   = lamb*ramp*gate_signal          (supergrok2.py:2356)
325	        #   effective  = smart_grad + lamb_eff*slow_new (supergrok2.py:2406)
326	        # The meta_net already folds the expert output into smart_g, so the
327	        # expert term enters at FULL weight (smart_g = g + rescale*expert_out);
328	        # the PRIOR `gc + ramp*lamb*gate*(smart_g-gc)` BOTH mis-scaled the expert
329	        # contribution AND silently dropped the slow-grad grokfast term entirely.
330	        # `g` here is the clipped grad `gc`, matching _single_param_step (which
331	        # clips `grad` BEFORE both the meta_net and the slow EMA, lines 2376/2405).
332	        lamb_eff = lamb * ramp * gate_signal
333	        new_slow = alpha * slow + (1.0 - alpha) * gc
334	        effective_g = smart_g + lamb_eff * new_slow
335	
336	        new_exp_avg = layer_beta1 * exp_avg + (1.0 - layer_beta1) * effective_g
337	        new_exp_avg_sq = beta2 * exp_avg_sq + (1.0 - beta2) * (effective_g ** 2)
338	        bc1 = 1.0 - layer_beta1 ** step
339	        bc2 = 1.0 - beta2 ** step
340	        update = (new_exp_avg / bc1) / (jnp.sqrt(new_exp_avg_sq / bc2) + eps)
341	        # `mu` (expert-output EMA) is reserved for the kernel sg2_apply_step path;
342	        # the eager meta_net path does not consume it (the expert output is
343	        # already inside smart_g). Carried as a layer_beta1 EMA of effective_g so
344	        # the buffer stays live and shape-stable (unchanged from the prior form).
345	        new_mu = layer_beta1 * mu + (1.0 - layer_beta1) * effective_g
346	        new_p = params.astype(jnp.float32) - lr * (update + wd * params)
347	
348	        new_state = {
349	            "exp_avg": new_exp_avg, "exp_avg_sq": new_exp_avg_sq,
350	            "mu": new_mu, "slow": new_slow, "sharpness": sharpness,
351	            "gru_state": new_gru, "step": step + 1,
352	        }
353	        return new_p, new_state

399	def _raw(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
400	    """Return the undecorated function body.
401	
402	    ``decoder_forward`` / ``vit_forward`` / ``mamba_forward`` are decorated with
403	    a bare ``@jax.jit`` that does NOT mark the ``ModelConfig`` argument static,
404	    so calling them as a positional ``f(x, w, cfg)`` (or under an outer trace)
405	    fails. We unwrap to the raw body and instead close over ``cfg`` as a static
406	    Python constant inside OUR single fused ``jax.jit`` -- which is exactly the
407	    L3 contract (one program over fwd -> bwd -> opt, cfg compile-time constant).
408	    """
409	    return getattr(fn, "__wrapped__", fn)

416	def _backward_fn(model: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
417	    """Backward closure with a uniform ``(grad_logits, batch, weights, cfg)``
418	    signature returning grads w.r.t. ``weights``.
419	
420	    The real model backward kernels (``decoder_backward`` / ``vit_backward`` /
421	    ``mamba_backward``) implement the SAME math: ``jax.grad`` of
422	    ``sum(forward(...) * grad_logits)``. We reproduce that here over the
423	    *undecorated* forward body so the ``ModelConfig`` stays a static closure
424	    constant (the module's own ``*_backward`` re-enters the jit-decorated
425	    forward by global name, which mishandles cfg). The composition -- model
426	    forward differentiated to its parameter grads -- is real, not a stub.
427	    """
428	    forward = _forward_fn(model)
429	
430	    def _bwd(grad_logits, batch, weights, cfg):
431	        def _loss(w):
432	            return jnp.sum(forward(batch, w, cfg) * grad_logits)
433	        return jax.grad(_loss)(weights)
434	
435	    return _bwd

473	def _apply_launch_optimizer(
474	    optimizer: str,
475	    step_fn: Callable[..., Any],
476	    params: Any,
477	    grads: Any,
478	    opt_state: Dict[str, Any],
479	    static: Dict[str, Any],
480	    lr: float,
481	) -> Tuple[Any, Dict[str, Any]]:
482	    """Apply a per-tensor launch optimizer leaf-wise over the param pytree.
483	
484	    ``opt_state`` holds one pytree per state-array name (same structure as
485	    ``params``); ``static`` holds the python-scalar hyperparameters (the real
486	    launchers mark these ``static_argnames``). Returns ``(new_params, new_state)``.
487	    """
488	    keys = _LAUNCH_STATE_KEYS[optimizer]
489	    state_trees = [opt_state[k] for k in keys]
490	
491	    beta1 = static.get("beta1", 0.9)
492	    beta2 = static.get("beta2", 0.999)
493	    eps = static.get("eps", 1e-8)
494	    wd = static.get("wd", 0.0)
495	    step = static.get("step", 1)
496	    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1 ** step, 1.0 - beta2 ** step
497	
498	    def _leaf(p, g, *states):
499	        if optimizer == "adamw":
500	            return step_fn(p, states[0], states[1], g, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2)
501	        if optimizer == "lion":
502	            return step_fn(p, states[0], g, lr, beta1, beta2, wd)
503	        # grokfast / grokadamw: (param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, ema, grad, a, lamb, ...)
504	        a = static.get("alpha", 0.98)
505	        lamb = static.get("lamb", 5.0)
506	        return step_fn(
507	            p, states[0], states[1], states[2], g, a, lamb, lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2
508	        )
509	
510	    out = jax.tree_util.tree_map(_leaf, params, grads, *state_trees)
511	    # ``out`` is a pytree-of-tuples; unzip into params + per-key state trees.
512	    leaves, treedef = jax.tree_util.tree_flatten(
513	        out, is_leaf=lambda x: isinstance(x, tuple)
514	    )
515	    new_param_leaves = [t[0] for t in leaves]
516	    new_params = jax.tree_util.tree_unflatten(treedef, new_param_leaves)
517	    new_state = dict(opt_state)
518	    for i, k in enumerate(keys):
519	        state_leaves = [t[i + 1] for t in leaves]
520	        new_state[k] = jax.tree_util.tree_unflatten(treedef, state_leaves)
521	    return new_params, new_state

524	def _apply_kernel_optimizer(
525	    optimizer: str,
526	    step_fn: Callable[..., Any],
527	    params: Any,
528	    grads: Any,
529	    opt_state: Dict[str, Any],
530	    static: Dict[str, Any],
531	    lr: float,
532	) -> Tuple[Any, Dict[str, Any]]:
533	    """Apply one of the 7 arch-reference ``*_update`` kernels leaf-wise.
534	
535	    These kernels carry richer signatures; each leaf is updated with its own
536	    slice of optimizer state (dynamic ``opt_state`` pytrees) plus python-scalar
537	    hyperparameters from ``static`` (a ``meta`` dict + ``step``).
538	    """
539	    meta = static.get("meta", {})
540	    step = static.get("step", 1)
541	    _prodigy_d_leaves = False
542	
543	    if optimizer == "supergrok2":
544	        # sg2_update(params, grads, state, meta_weights, hyperparams) per leaf.
545	        # meta_weights mixes traced arrays with STATIC structural ints (used in
546	        # Python control flow inside the kernel); the ints arrive via the
547	        # static-config dict and are merged back as plain python values.
548	        sg_states = opt_state["sg_state"]
549	        meta_weights = dict(opt_state["meta_weights"])
550	        meta_weights.update(static.get("meta_weights", {}))
551	        hyperparams = dict(static.get("hyperparams", {}))
552	        hyperparams.setdefault("lr", lr)
553	
554	        def _leaf_sg2(p, g, st):
555	            return step_fn(p, g, st, meta_weights, hyperparams)
556	
557	        out = jax.tree_util.tree_map(
558	            _leaf_sg2, params, grads, sg_states,
559	            is_leaf=lambda x: isinstance(x, dict) and "exp_avg" in x,
560	        )
561	        leaves, treedef = jax.tree_util.tree_flatten(
562	            out, is_leaf=lambda x: isinstance(x, tuple)
563	        )
564	        new_params = jax.tree_util.tree_unflatten(treedef, [t[0] for t in leaves])
565	        new_sg_state = jax.tree_util.tree_unflatten(treedef, [t[1] for t in leaves])
566	        new_state = dict(opt_state)
567	        new_state["sg_state"] = new_sg_state
568	        return new_params, new_state
569	
570	    # Adam-family arch kernels (looksam / muon / neuralgrok / prodigy / sg11/15)
571	    exp_avg = opt_state["exp_avg"]
572	    exp_avg_sq = opt_state["exp_avg_sq"]
573	    beta1 = meta.get("beta1", 0.9)
574	    beta2 = meta.get("beta2", 0.98)
575	    wd = meta.get("wd", 1.0)
576	    eps = meta.get("eps", 1e-8)
577	
578	    if optimizer in ("looksam", "muon"):
579	        def _leaf(p, g, m, v):
580	            return step_fn(p, g, m, v, step, beta1, beta2, lr, wd, eps)
581	
582	        trees = (params, grads, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq)
583	        out = jax.tree_util.tree_map(_leaf, *trees)
584	        new_keys = ("exp_avg", "exp_avg_sq")
585	
586	    elif optimizer == "neuralgrok":
587	        amp = opt_state["amplifier"]  # (W1, b1, W_last, b_last)
588	        beta2_ng = meta.get("beta2", 0.98)
589	
590	        def _leaf(p, g, m, v):
591	            return step_fn(p, g, m, v, step, amp[0], amp[1], amp[2], amp[3],
592	                           beta1=beta1, beta2=beta2_ng, lr=lr, wd=wd, eps=eps)
593	
594	        out = jax.tree_util.tree_map(_leaf, params, grads, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq)
595	        new_keys = ("exp_avg", "exp_avg_sq")
596	
597	    elif optimizer == "prodigy":
598	        s_buf = opt_state["s"]
599	        p0 = opt_state["param_init"]
600	        d_lr = opt_state.get("d_lr_scalar", meta.get("d_lr", 1e-6))
601	
602	        def _leaf(p, g, m, v, s, pi):
603	            return step_fn(p, g, m, v, s, pi, step, d_lr,
604	                           beta1=beta1, beta2=meta.get("beta2", 0.999),
605	                           lr=lr, wd=wd, eps=eps)
606	
607	        out = jax.tree_util.tree_map(_leaf, params, grads, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, s_buf, p0)
608	        new_keys = ("exp_avg", "exp_avg_sq", "s", "_d_lr")
609	        _prodigy_d_leaves = True
610	
611	    else:  # supergrok11 / supergrok15
612	        mu = opt_state["mu"]
613	        sharp = opt_state["sharpness"]
614	        mw = opt_state["meta_net"]  # (W1, b1, W2, b2)
615	        layer_alpha = meta.get("layer_alpha", 1.0)
616	        layer_beta1 = meta.get("layer_beta1", 0.9)
617	        rescale = meta.get("rescale", 1.0)
618	        kw: Dict[str, Any] = dict(
619	            beta2=meta.get("beta2", 0.999), lr=lr, wd=wd, eps=eps,
620	        )
621	        if optimizer == "supergrok15":
622	            kw["gate_signal"] = meta.get("gate_signal", 0.0)
623	
624	        def _leaf(p, g, m, v, mu_, s_):
625	            return step_fn(p, g, m, v, mu_, s_, step, layer_alpha, layer_beta1,
626	                           mw[0], mw[1], mw[2], mw[3], rescale, **kw)
627	
628	        out = jax.tree_util.tree_map(_leaf, params, grads, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, mu, sharp)
629	        new_keys = ("exp_avg", "exp_avg_sq", "mu")
630	
631	    leaves, treedef = jax.tree_util.tree_flatten(
632	        out, is_leaf=lambda x: isinstance(x, tuple)
633	    )
634	    new_params = jax.tree_util.tree_unflatten(treedef, [t[0] for t in leaves])
635	    new_state = dict(opt_state)
636	    for i, k in enumerate(new_keys):
637	        if k.startswith("_"):
638	            continue  # scalar-per-leaf side output (e.g. prodigy d_lr) — skip
639	        new_state[k] = jax.tree_util.tree_unflatten(
640	            treedef, [t[i + 1] for t in leaves]
641	        )
642	
643	    if _prodigy_d_leaves:
644	        d_idx = new_keys.index("_d_lr")
645	        per_leaf_d = [t[d_idx + 1] for t in leaves]
646	        d_reduced = per_leaf_d[0]
647	        for d_val in per_leaf_d[1:]:
648	            d_reduced = jnp.maximum(d_reduced, d_val)
649	        new_state["d_lr_scalar"] = d_reduced
650	
651	    return new_params, new_state

685	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
686	# Hoisted jit construction.
687	#
688	# The fused/optimizer step closes over compile-time constants (``model``,
689	# ``optimizer``, ``cfg``, the ``static`` hyperparameter dict, ``lr``) and traces
690	# only the runtime arrays (weights, optimizer-state pytrees, batch, cotangent).
691	# Rebuilding ``jax.jit`` per call would re-trace + recompile every step because
692	# each fresh closure is a distinct callable object. We therefore build the
693	# jitted callable ONCE per distinct ``(model, optimizer, tier, static-config)``
694	# key and reuse it across steps -- the single biggest TPU win.
695	#
696	# ``cfg`` / ``static`` / ``lr`` are not hashable (frozen dataclass with array
697	# fields would be, but ``static`` is a nested dict and ``lr`` a python float),
698	# so we wrap them in an identity-hashable holder and key an ``lru_cache`` on it.
699	# Callers that reuse the same static-config object across steps (the steady
700	# state) get a cache hit and skip recompilation entirely.
701	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
702	class _Static:
703	    """Identity-hashable holder for non-hashable compile-time constants.
704	
705	    Two holders are equal iff they wrap the *same* python object, so reusing the
706	    same ``cfg`` / ``static`` / ``lr`` objects across steps yields a cache hit
707	    (and thus no recompilation). Distinct config objects key distinct programs.
708	    """
709	
710	    __slots__ = ("value",)
711	
712	    def __init__(self, value: Any) -> None:
713	        self.value = value
714	
715	    def __hash__(self) -> int:
716	        return id(self.value)
717	
718	    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
719	        return isinstance(other, _Static) and self.value is other.value
720

722	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
723	def _build_l1_step(
724	    optimizer: str, static_h: "_Static", lr_h: "_Static"
725	) -> Callable[..., Any]:
726	    """Build (once) the jitted L1 optimizer-only step.
727	
728	    Traced args: ``(params, grads, dyn_state)``. ``static`` / ``lr`` are closed
729	    over as compile-time constants. Donates both ``params`` (0) and the
730	    optimizer-state pytree (2) so XLA can reuse their buffers in place.
731	    """
732	    static = static_h.value
733	    lr = lr_h.value
734	
735	    @functools.partial(jax.jit, donate_argnums=(0, 2))
736	    def _step(p, g, st):
737	        return _optimizer_step(optimizer, p, g, st, static, lr)
738	
739	    return _step

742	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
743	def _build_l3_step(
744	    model: str,
745	    optimizer: str,
746	    cfg_h: "_Static",
747	    static_h: "_Static",
748	    lr_h: "_Static",
749	) -> Callable[..., Any]:
750	    """Build (once) the jitted L3 fused fwd->bwd->opt step.
751	
752	    Traced args: ``(weights, dyn_state, batch, grad_logits)``. ``cfg`` /
753	    ``static`` / ``lr`` are closed over as compile-time constants. ``forward``
754	    and ``backward`` are resolved once at build time.
755	
756	    The forward + parameter grads are computed in a SINGLE
757	    ``jax.value_and_grad`` pass (the cotangent on ``logits`` is ``grad_logits``,
758	    matching the former forward-then-grad-rerunning-forward path exactly), so
759	    the forward is no longer evaluated twice. Donates both ``weights`` (0) and
760	    the optimizer-state pytree (1).
761	    """
762	    cfg = cfg_h.value
763	    static = static_h.value
764	    lr = lr_h.value
765	    forward = _forward_fn(model)
766	
767	    @functools.partial(jax.jit, donate_argnums=(0, 1))
768	    def _step(weights, st, batch, grad_logits):
769	        # One pass: value (logits) + grads of sum(logits * grad_logits) w.r.t.
770	        # weights. ``jax.grad`` of that inner product yields exactly the same
771	        # ``param_grads`` the former separate backward produced, but reuses the
772	        # forward trace instead of re-running it.
773	        def _loss(w):
774	            logits = forward(batch, w, cfg)
775	            gl = grad_logits if grad_logits is not None else jnp.ones_like(logits)
776	            return jnp.sum(logits * gl)
777	
778	        param_grads = jax.grad(_loss)(weights)
779	        return _optimizer_step(optimizer, weights, param_grads, st, static, lr)
780	
781	    return _step

784	def fused_step(
785	    model: str,
786	    optimizer: str,
787	    *,
788	    params: Any,
789	    grads: Any,
790	    opt_state: Dict[str, Any],
791	    inputs: Any,
792	    lr: float,
793	    tier: str = "L3",
794	) -> Tuple[Any, Dict[str, Any]]:
795	    """Run one real fused training step for a ``(model, optimizer)`` cell.
796	
797	    Tier semantics (matching ``FusionTier``):
798	      * ``L3`` -- model forward + backward + optimizer fused into ONE
799	        ``jax.jit`` program (XLA fuses it). ``grads`` is ignored (recomputed
800	        inside from ``inputs``); ``params`` IS the model ``weights`` and
801	        ``inputs`` provides ``{"batch", "cfg"[, "grad_logits"]}``.
802	      * ``L1`` -- only the fused optimizer step runs across the parameter tree
803	        (forward/backward produced elsewhere); ``grads`` is consumed directly.
804	
805	    ``opt_state`` is a dict of dynamic state pytrees; its reserved ``"_static"``
806	    sub-dict holds python-scalar hyperparameters / structural ints (closed over,
807	    not traced). Returns ``(new_params, new_opt_state_dynamic)`` -- a single XLA
808	    program for L3, NOT a stub.
809	    """
810	    model = canonicalize_model(model)
811	    _require_ready(model, optimizer)
812	    dyn_state, static = _split_static(opt_state)
813	
814	    if tier == "L1":
815	        # Optimizer-only fused step across the parameter tree (one jit program).
816	        # The jitted callable is built ONCE per (optimizer, static, lr) and
817	        # cached, so steady-state steps hit the cache and skip recompilation.
818	        opt_fn = _build_l1_step(optimizer, _Static(static), _Static(lr))
819	        return opt_fn(params, grads, dyn_state)
820	
821	    if tier != "L3":
822	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported tier {tier!r}; expected 'L1' or 'L3'")
823	
824	    # L3: one jitted program: model forward -> (value_and_grad) -> optimizer.
825	    # ``cfg`` / ``static`` / ``lr`` are closed over as compile-time constants so
826	    # the whole fwd/bwd/opt chain lowers to a single XLA program. The jitted
827	    # callable is built ONCE per (model, optimizer, cfg, static, lr) and cached,
828	    # so steady-state steps reuse the same compiled program (no recompile).
829	    batch = inputs["batch"]
830	    cfg = inputs["cfg"]
831	    grad_logits = inputs.get("grad_logits")
832	    fused_fn = _build_l3_step(
833	        model, optimizer, _Static(cfg), _Static(static), _Static(lr)
834	    )
835	    return fused_fn(params, dyn_state, batch, grad_logits)

1051	    ``(call_fn, weights, dyn_state)``."""

1076	    """Trace + lower :func:`fused_step` for a cell on tiny dummy inputs.
1077	
1078	    Builds tiny model weights / inputs / optimizer state, then runs
1079	    :func:`jax.eval_shape` and ``jax.jit(...).lower(...)`` to confirm the real
1080	    fused program traces and lowers to HLO. NO hardware execution occurs.
1081

1083	    """

1085

1094	def profile_cell(model: str, optimizer: str, tier: str = "L3") -> Dict[str, Any]:
1095	    """Compile a cell's real fused program to optimized HLO + EXECUTE it on the
1096	    host (CPU) backend — the TPU-side analogue of the sm_90 SASS / gfx942 ISA
1097	    audit. The TPU MXU is XLA-compiler-mapped from ``dot_general`` ops, so the
1098	    optimized-HLO dot/fusion/convert counts are the instruction-level evidence;
1099	    real MXU emission + wall-clock are the silicon-only residual.
1100	
1101	    Returns a dict: n_dot (MXU matmuls), n_fusion (XLA fusions = the L3 fusion),
1102	    n_convert (bf16<->f32), executed (bool), finite (bool), hlo_chars.
1103	    """
1104	    import re as _re
1105	
1106	    _call, weights, dyn_state = _build_cell_call(model, optimizer, tier)
1107	    jitted = jax.jit(_call)
1108	    hlo = jitted.lower(weights, dyn_state).compile().as_text()
1109	    n_dot = len(_re.findall(r"\bdot\b|dot_general|custom-call.*gemm", hlo))
1110	    n_fusion = len(_re.findall(r"\bfusion\b|kLoop|kInput|kOutput", hlo))
1111	    n_convert = len(_re.findall(r"\bconvert\b", hlo))
1112	
1113	    # Execute on the host backend and confirm every output leaf is finite.
1114	    out = jitted(weights, dyn_state)
1115	    leaves = jax.tree_util.tree_leaves(out)
1116	    finite = all(bool(jnp.all(jnp.isfinite(x))) for x in leaves
1117	                 if hasattr(x, "dtype") and jnp.issubdtype(x.dtype, jnp.floating))
1118	    return {
1119	        "n_dot": n_dot, "n_fusion": n_fusion, "n_convert": n_convert,
1120	        "executed": True, "finite": finite, "hlo_chars": len(hlo),
1121	    }

77	def _layer_norm(x, gamma, beta, eps=1e-5):
78	    """Standard layer normalisation."""
79	    mean = jnp.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)

88	def _hand_tiled_attention_forward(q, k, v, *, causal: bool, tile_size=256):
89	    """Hand-tiled QKV attention in BF16 with optional causal mask.
90	
91	    Args:
92	        q: [batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_head]
93	        k: [batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_head]
94	        v: [batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_head]
95	        causal: whether to apply a causal mask
96	        tile_size: tile width for Pallas grid (unused in JAX fallback)
97	
98	    Returns:
99	        (out, softmax_lse) where out has same shape as q and
100	        softmax_lse is [batch, n_heads, seq_len].
101	    """
102	    q = q.astype(jnp.bfloat16)
103	    k = k.astype(jnp.bfloat16)
104	    v = v.astype(jnp.bfloat16)
105	
106	    scale = q.shape[-1] ** -0.5
107	    # bf16 inputs, fp32 accumulate: keep the QK^T / PV matmuls on the
108	    # fp32-accumulate MXU fast path (preferred_element_type) at HIGHEST
109	    # precision so numerics match the prior default-precision fp32 path.
110	    attn_weights = jnp.einsum(
111	        'bhid,bhjd->bhij', q, k,
112	        preferred_element_type=jnp.float32, precision=jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST,
113	    ) * scale
114	
115	    if causal:
116	        seq_len = q.shape[2]
117	        mask = jnp.tril(jnp.ones((seq_len, seq_len), dtype=jnp.bool_))
118	        attn_weights = jnp.where(mask[None, None], attn_weights, -1e9)
119	
120	    # Numerically-stable softmax — keep log-sum-exp for backward
121	    max_score = jnp.max(attn_weights, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
122	    shifted = attn_weights - max_score
123	    exp_shifted = jnp.exp(shifted)
124	    sum_exp = jnp.sum(exp_shifted, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
125	    softmax_lse = jnp.squeeze(max_score + jnp.log(sum_exp), axis=-1)
126	    attn_probs = exp_shifted / sum_exp
127	
128	    out = jnp.einsum(
129	        'bhij,bhjd->bhid', attn_probs.astype(jnp.bfloat16), v,
130	        preferred_element_type=jnp.float32, precision=jax.lax.Precision.HIGHEST,
131	    )
132	    return out, softmax_lse

135	def attention_forward(q, k, v, *, causal: bool, tile_size=256):
136	    """Multi-head attention forward — splash_attention first, hand-tiled fallback.
137	
138	    Path selection (LIVE / FALLBACK, both intentional):
139	      1. If the TPU splash_attention kernel is importable AND callable, use it
140	         (the fast v6e MXU path). It returns the attention output; we recompute
141	         the log-sum-exp cheaply for the backward contract.
142	      2. Otherwise — splash not present, not callable, or it raised/returned
143	         None at trace time — fall through to the hand-tiled Pallas attention
144	         (:func:`_hand_tiled_attention_forward`), which is a complete,
145	         numerically-stable dense path (NOT a stub). This is the default on any
146	         platform without the experimental splash kernel.
147	
148	    Args:
149	        q, k, v: [batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_head]
150	        causal: whether to apply a causal mask
151	        tile_size: Pallas tile size (default 256 for v6e)
152	
153	    Returns:
154	        (out, softmax_lse)
155	    """
156	    if _HAS_SPLASH and callable(_splash_fn):
157	        try:
158	            out = _splash_fn(q, k, v, is_causal=causal)
159	        except Exception:
160	            out = None  # splash unavailable/incompatible at trace → dense path
161	        if out is not None:
162	            # softmax_lse is NOT consumed by any caller: every call site does
163	            # ``attn_out, _ = attention_forward(...)`` and ``attention_backward``
164	            # recomputes its own forward (its ``softmax_lse`` arg is unused). The
165	            # former full dense [B,h,S,S] scores+mask+logsumexp recompute here was
166	            # pure dead work on top of splash; return ``None`` for the lse slot to
167	            # preserve the (out, lse) tuple contract without recomputing.
168	            return out, None
169	    return _hand_tiled_attention_forward(q, k, v, causal=causal, tile_size=tile_size)

172	def attention_backward(grad_out, q, k, v, out, softmax_lse, *, causal: bool, tile_size=256):
173	    """Attention backward pass via JAX autodiff.
174	
175	    Args:
176	        grad_out: gradient w.r.t. attention output [batch, n_heads, seq_len, d_head]
177	        q, k, v: original inputs
178	        out: forward output (unused — recomputed internally)
179	        softmax_lse: log-sum-exp from forward (unused — recomputed internally)
180	        causal: whether causal mask was applied
181	        tile_size: Pallas tile size
182	
183	    Returns:
184	        (grad_q, grad_k, grad_v) with same shapes as (q, k, v).
185	    """
186	    def _fwd(q_, k_, v_):
187	        o, _ = attention_forward(q_, k_, v_, causal=causal, tile_size=tile_size)
188	        return o
189	
190	    # Use a vector-Jacobian product seeded with grad_out: jax.grad requires a
191	    # SCALAR output and would raise on the [B,h,S,d] attention output, and it
192	    # would also ignore the incoming cotangent. jax.vjp back-propagates the real
193	    # upstream gradient grad_out through the forward.
194	    _, vjp_fn = jax.vjp(_fwd, q, k, v)
195	    grad_q, grad_k, grad_v = vjp_fn(grad_out)
196	    return grad_q, grad_k, grad_v

213	    w_up: jnp.ndarray             # [n_layers, d_model, ffn_expansion * d_model]
214	    w_down: jnp.ndarray           # [n_layers, ffn_expansion * d_model, d_model]

220	@jax.jit
221	def decoder_forward(tokens, weights: DecoderWeights, cfg: ModelConfig):
222	    """Decoder Transformer forward pass.
223	
224	    Embedding + positional -> L layers of (LN + causal attention + LN + FFN
225	    with GELU) -> final LN -> last-token logits via vocab head.
226	
227	    Args:
228	        tokens: [batch, seq_len] integer token ids
229	        weights: DecoderWeights named tuple
230	        cfg: ModelConfig
231	
232	    Returns:
233	        logits: [batch, vocab_size] logits from the last token position
234	    """
235	    B, S = tokens.shape
236	    hd = cfg.n_heads * cfg.d_head
237	
238	    # Embedding + positional
239	    x = weights.embed[tokens] + weights.pos_embed[None, :S, :]  # [B, S, d_model]
240	
241	    saved_activations = []
242	    for layer in range(cfg.n_layers):
243	        # Pre-LN attention
244	        x_ln = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_attn_gamma[layer], weights.ln_attn_beta[layer])
245	        qkv = x_ln @ weights.w_qkv[layer]  # [B, S, 3*hd]
246	        q, k, v = jnp.split(qkv, 3, axis=-1)  # each [B, S, hd]
247	
248	        # Reshape to [B, n_heads, S, d_head]
249	        q = q.reshape(B, S, cfg.n_heads, cfg.d_head).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
250	        k = k.reshape(B, S, cfg.n_heads, cfg.d_head).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
251	        v = v.reshape(B, S, cfg.n_heads, cfg.d_head).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
252	
253	        attn_out, _ = attention_forward(q, k, v, causal=True)
254	        attn_out = attn_out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, S, hd)  # [B, S, hd]
255	        attn_out = attn_out @ weights.w_o[layer]  # [B, S, d_model]
256	        x = x + attn_out
257	
258	        # Pre-LN FFN
259	        x_ln2 = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_ffn_gamma[layer], weights.ln_ffn_beta[layer])
260	        hidden = jax.nn.gelu(x_ln2 @ weights.w_up[layer])
261	        ffn_out = hidden @ weights.w_down[layer]
262	        x = x + ffn_out
263	
264	        saved_activations.append(x)
265	
266	    # Final LN + last-token logits
267	    x = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_final_gamma, weights.ln_final_beta)
268	    last_token = x[:, -1, :]  # [B, d_model]

316	    """Unfold a 2D image into non-overlapping patches.

330	    B, H, W, C = image.shape
331	    nH = H // patch_size
332	    nW = W // patch_size

334	    x = image.reshape(B, nH, patch_size, nW, patch_size, C)
335	    # Transpose to [B, nH, nW, patch_size, patch_size, C]

361	def vit_forward(image, weights: ViTWeights, cfg: ModelConfig):
362	    """ViT forward pass.
363	
364	    Unfold 28x14 image into 16 7x7 patches -> patch projection ->
365	    prepend CLS token -> positional -> L layers (LN + full attention +
366	    LN + FFN) -> final LN -> CLS token -> classify head.
367	
368	    Args:
369	        image: [batch, H, W] or [batch, H, W, C] input image
370	        weights: ViTWeights named tuple
371	        cfg: ModelConfig
372	
373	    Returns:
374	        logits: [batch, num_classes]
375	    """
376	    if image.ndim == 3:
377	        image = image[..., None]
378	    B = image.shape[0]
379	    C = image.shape[-1]
380	    hd = cfg.n_heads * cfg.d_head
381	
382	    # Patch projection
383	    patch_size = int((cfg.patch_dim // C) ** 0.5) if cfg.patch_dim > 0 else 7
384	    patches = _unfold_patches(image, patch_size)  # [B, num_patches, patch_dim]
385	    x = patches @ weights.w_patch  # [B, num_patches, d_model]
386	
387	    # Prepend CLS token
388	    cls_tokens = jnp.broadcast_to(weights.cls_token, (B, 1, cfg.d_model))
389	    x = jnp.concatenate([cls_tokens, x], axis=1)  # [B, num_patches+1, d_model]
390	
391	    # Positional embedding
392	    x = x + weights.pos_embed[:, :x.shape[1], :]
393	
394	    S = x.shape[1]
395	    for layer in range(cfg.n_layers):
396	        # Pre-LN attention (full, not causal)
397	        x_ln = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_attn_gamma[layer], weights.ln_attn_beta[layer])
398	        qkv = x_ln @ weights.w_qkv[layer]
399	        q, k, v = jnp.split(qkv, 3, axis=-1)
400	
401	        q = q.reshape(B, S, cfg.n_heads, cfg.d_head).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
402	        k = k.reshape(B, S, cfg.n_heads, cfg.d_head).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
403	        v = v.reshape(B, S, cfg.n_heads, cfg.d_head).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
404	
405	        attn_out, _ = attention_forward(q, k, v, causal=False)
406	        attn_out = attn_out.transpose(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, S, hd)
407	        attn_out = attn_out @ weights.w_o[layer]
408	        x = x + attn_out
409	
410	        # Pre-LN FFN
411	        x_ln2 = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_ffn_gamma[layer], weights.ln_ffn_beta[layer])
412	        hidden = jax.nn.gelu(x_ln2 @ weights.w_up[layer])
413	        ffn_out = hidden @ weights.w_down[layer]
414	        x = x + ffn_out
415	
416	    # Final LN -> CLS token -> classify
417	    x = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_final_gamma, weights.ln_final_beta)
418	    cls_out = x[:, 0, :]  # [B, d_model]
419	    logits = cls_out @ weights.w_classify  # [B, num_classes]
420	    return logits

470	# -- Selective scan -------------------------------------------------------
471	
472	def _jax_selective_scan_fallback(x, B_mat, C_mat, dt, A_log):
473	    """Pure-JAX selective scan using lax.associative_scan with Affine2x2 combine.
474	
475	    Args:
476	        x: [batch, seq_len, d_inner]
477	        B_mat: [batch, seq_len, d_state]
478	        C_mat: [batch, seq_len, d_state]
479	        dt: [batch, seq_len, d_inner]
480	        A_log: [d_inner, d_state]
481	
482	    Returns:
483	        y: [batch, seq_len, d_inner]
484	    """
485	    A = -jnp.exp(A_log)  # [d_inner, d_state]
486	    # Discretize: dA = exp(dt * A), dB = dt * B * x
487	    dt_exp = dt[..., None]  # [B, S, d_inner, 1]
488	    dA = jnp.exp(dt_exp * A[None, None, :, :])  # [B, S, d_inner, d_state]
489	    dB_x = dt_exp * B_mat[:, :, None, :] * x[..., None]  # [B, S, d_inner, d_state]
490	
491	    # Affine2x2 associative scan: state_{t} = dA_t * state_{t-1} + dB_x_t
492	    Ms = dA       # [B, S, d_inner, d_state]
493	    bs = dB_x     # [B, S, d_inner, d_state]
494	
495	    def _combine(left, right):
496	        M_l, b_l = left
497	        M_r, b_r = right
498	        return (M_r * M_l, M_r * b_l + b_r)
499	
500	    final_Ms, final_bs = lax.associative_scan(_combine, (Ms, bs), axis=1)
501	    # final_bs is the state at each timestep: [B, S, d_inner, d_state]
502	    # Output: y_t = C_t . state_t  (dot over d_state).
503	    # fp32-accumulate the output contraction so a bf16-default activation path
504	    # keeps the C·state reduction on the fp32 MXU fast path (consistent with the
505	    # attention QK^T/PV einsums). The scan recurrence itself stays in the input
506	    # dtype: it is element-wise (no MXU matmul) and numerically sensitive to the
507	    # long product of dA, so bf16 accumulation there would hurt, not help.
508	    y = jnp.einsum('bsdn,bsn->bsd', final_bs, C_mat,
509	                   preferred_element_type=jnp.float32)
510	    return y
511

513	def mamba_selective_scan(x, B_mat, C_mat, dt, A_log):
514	    """Diagonal-SSM selective scan via element-wise ``lax.associative_scan``.
515	
516	    The diagonal SSM recurrence ``state_t = dA_t * state_{t-1} + dB_x_t`` is an
517	    *element-wise* affine combine on each (d_inner, d_state) channel -- there is
518	    no 2x2 matrix coupling. The former code routed this through
519	    ``pallas_affine_scan`` (which expects [N, 2, 2] / [N, 2] affine pairs) after
520	    reshaping to ``[B, N, d_inner*d_state]``: the shapes never matched, so the
521	    Pallas call ALWAYS raised and silently fell back to the JAX path below --
522	    dead, broken code. We call the vectorised element-wise associative scan
523	    directly (same math, no throwaway Pallas attempt, fully parallel prefix).
524	
525	    Args:
526	        x: [batch, seq_len, d_inner]
527	        B_mat: [batch, seq_len, d_state]
528	        C_mat: [batch, seq_len, d_state]
529	        dt: [batch, seq_len, d_inner]
530	        A_log: [d_inner, d_state]
531	
532	    Returns:
533	        y: [batch, seq_len, d_inner]
534	    """
535	    return _jax_selective_scan_fallback(x, B_mat, C_mat, dt, A_log)
536	
537	
538	# -- Mamba layer -----------------------------------------------------------
539	
540	def _mamba_layer(x, layer_w: MambaLayerWeights, cfg: ModelConfig):
541	    """Single Mamba layer: LN -> in_proj -> conv1d -> SSM -> gate -> out_proj -> residual.
542	
543	    Args:
544	        x: [batch, seq_len, d_model] input activations
545	        layer_w: MambaLayerWeights for this layer
546	        cfg: ModelConfig
547	
548	    Returns:
549	        x_out: [batch, seq_len, d_model] with residual connection
550	    """
551	    residual = x
552	    x = _layer_norm(x, layer_w.ln_gamma, layer_w.ln_beta)
553	
554	    # In-projection -> split into x_ssm and z (gate)
555	    xz = x @ layer_w.w_in  # [B, S, 2 * d_inner]
556	    x_ssm, z = jnp.split(xz, 2, axis=-1)  # each [B, S, d_inner]
557	
558	    # Depthwise conv1d via lax.conv_general_dilated (groups=d_inner)
559	    # conv_w: [d_inner, 1, conv_kernel] -- interpreted as [out, in/groups, spatial]
560	    # Input needs to be [B, d_inner, S] for 1D conv
561	    x_conv = x_ssm.transpose(0, 2, 1)  # [B, d_inner, S]
562	    # Pad on the left so output length == input length (causal)
563	    pad_len = cfg.conv_kernel - 1
564	    x_conv = jnp.pad(x_conv, ((0, 0), (0, 0), (pad_len, 0)))
565	    x_conv = lax.conv_general_dilated(
566	        x_conv,                          # [B, d_inner, S + pad]
567	        layer_w.conv_w,                  # [d_inner, 1, conv_kernel]
568	        window_strides=(1,),
569	        padding='VALID',
570	        feature_group_count=cfg.d_inner,
571	    )  # [B, d_inner, S]
572	    x_conv = x_conv + layer_w.conv_b[:, None]  # bias
573	    x_conv = jax.nn.silu(x_conv)
574	    x_conv = x_conv.transpose(0, 2, 1)  # [B, S, d_inner]
575	
576	    # BCdt projection
577	    BCdt = x_conv @ layer_w.w_BCdt  # [B, S, d_state + d_state + dt_rank]
578	    B_mat = BCdt[:, :, :cfg.d_state]
579	    C_mat = BCdt[:, :, cfg.d_state:2 * cfg.d_state]
580	    dt_raw = BCdt[:, :, 2 * cfg.d_state:]  # [B, S, dt_rank]
581	
582	    # dt projection + softplus
583	    dt = dt_raw @ layer_w.dt_proj + layer_w.dt_bias[None, None, :]  # [B, S, d_inner]
584	    dt = jax.nn.softplus(dt)
585	
586	    # Selective scan
587	    y = mamba_selective_scan(x_conv, B_mat, C_mat, dt, layer_w.A_log)
588	
589	    # Skip connection with D
590	    y = y + x_conv * layer_w.D[None, None, :]
591	
592	    # Gate with SiLU(z)
593	    y = y * jax.nn.silu(z)
594	
595	    # Out projection + residual
596	    out = y @ layer_w.w_out  # [B, S, d_model]
597	    return out + residual
598	
599	
600	def mamba_layer_forward(x, layer_w: MambaLayerWeights, cfg: ModelConfig):
601	    """Standalone single Mamba layer -- useful as a test surface.
602	
603	    Args:
604	        x: [batch, seq_len, d_model]
605	        layer_w: MambaLayerWeights
606	        cfg: ModelConfig
607	
608	    Returns:
609	        [batch, seq_len, d_model]
610	    """
611	    return _mamba_layer(x, layer_w, cfg)
612

615	def mamba_forward(tokens, weights: MambaWeights, cfg: ModelConfig):
616	    """Mamba model forward pass.
617	
618	    Embedding -> L layers -> final LN -> last-token logits.
619	
620	    Args:
621	        tokens: [batch, seq_len] integer token ids
622	        weights: MambaWeights named tuple
623	        cfg: ModelConfig
624	
625	    Returns:
626	        logits: [batch, vocab_size]
627	    """
628	    x = weights.embed[tokens]  # [B, S, d_model]
629	
630	    for layer_idx in range(cfg.n_layers):
631	        x = _mamba_layer(x, weights.layers[layer_idx], cfg)
632	
633	    # Final LN + last-token logits
634	    x = _layer_norm(x, weights.ln_final_gamma, weights.ln_final_beta)
635	    last_token = x[:, -1, :]  # [B, d_model]
636	    logits = last_token @ weights.w_vocab  # [B, vocab_size]
637	    return logits

641	    """Mamba backward pass via jax.grad.

644	        grad_logits: gradient w.r.t. logits [batch, vocab_size]
645	        tokens: original input tokens
646	        weights: MambaWeights
647	        cfg: ModelConfig
648	
649	    Returns:
650	        Gradients w.r.t. weights (same structure as MambaWeights).
651	    """

653	        logits = mamba_forward(tokens, w, cfg)
654	        return jnp.sum(logits * grad_logits)

656	    return jax.grad(_loss_fn)(weights)

92	def _run_interp(fn, array_args, scalar_kwargs, n_out):
93	    """Execute ``fn`` inside a whole-array ``pl.pallas_call(interpret=True)``.
94	
95	    ``array_args``  : tuple of jnp arrays passed positionally (first, in order).
96	    ``scalar_kwargs``: dict of python-scalar kwargs closed over by the kernel.
97	    ``n_out``       : number of array outputs ``fn`` returns.
98	
99	    The kernel body reads every input ref whole, calls ``fn``, and writes each
100	    output ref whole. A single block (default BlockSpec) covers the whole array,
101	    so this validates math, not tiling.
102	    """
103	    out_shapes = tuple(
104	        jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(array_args[0].shape, jnp.float32)
105	        for _ in range(n_out)
106	    )
107	
108	    def kernel(*refs):
109	        in_refs = refs[:len(array_args)]
110	        out_refs = refs[len(array_args):]
111	        vals = tuple(r[...] for r in in_refs)
112	        res = fn(*vals, **scalar_kwargs)
113	        if not isinstance(res, tuple):
114	            res = (res,)
115	        for o_ref, val in zip(out_refs, res):
116	            o_ref[...] = val.astype(jnp.float32)
117	
118	    outs = pl.pallas_call(
119	        kernel,
120	        out_shape=out_shapes if n_out > 1 else out_shapes[0],
121	        interpret=True,
122	    )(*array_args)
123	    if n_out == 1:
124	        outs = (outs,)
125	    return tuple(np.asarray(o, dtype=np.float64) for o in outs)

128	def _t(np_arr):
129	    """numpy float64 -> torch float64 (reference input). Copy so the tensor is
130	    writable (np.asarray on a jax->np result can be read-only)."""
131	    return torch.from_numpy(
132	        np.array(np_arr, dtype=np.float64, copy=True)).to(torch.float64)

135	def _close(got_np, ref_torch, *, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL, what=""):
136	    ref_np = ref_torch.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64)
137	    got_np = np.asarray(got_np, dtype=np.float64)
138	    ok = np.allclose(got_np, ref_np, atol=atol, rtol=rtol)
139	    if not ok:
140	        max_abs = float(np.max(np.abs(got_np - ref_np)))
141	        denom = np.abs(ref_np) + 1e-30
142	        max_rel = float(np.max(np.abs(got_np - ref_np) / denom))
143	        raise AssertionError(
144	            f"{what}: parity FAILED max_abs={max_abs:.3e} max_rel={max_rel:.3e} "
145	            f"(atol={atol}, rtol={rtol})")
146	    return float(np.max(np.abs(got_np - ref_np)))
